title: Effect of a length-counting action
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. Choose optional states $q,q'$, natural numbers $i,j,r,s$ with $i,j\le |x|$, signs $m,d\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and an optional bit $b$. Suppose moving the input head from position $i+1$ by $m$ gives position $j+1$, and $(r-1)+d=s-1$. Then applying the length-counting action that moves the input head by $m$, moves the extra work-tape head by $d$, emits $b$ if present, and enters state $q'$, to the length-counting configuration built from $c$ at input position $i$, state $q$, and extra-tape position $r$, gives the corresponding configuration at input position $j$, state $q'$, and extra-tape position $s$, with output equal to the one-bit word $b$ if present and empty otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: Configuration c of M on x
Natural numbers i, j, r, s
Input-head movement equality from i+1 to j+1
